source_version: Capella (continuously deployed, no discrete version number)

concepts.label: Monitoring dashboard metric graph (Capella UI)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - minted last round from monitoring-reference.json (a reference/ page that only linked to this page). This is the feature's own authoritative page, confirming the concept and giving it real structure: 5 named dashboards (Cluster Overview, Data Service, Index Service, Query Service, Node Metrics) plus a customizable Metrics Explorer, and per-timeframe chart resolution (60s at 30m/1h/2h, up to 3h buckets at 30d)

relations.subject: monitoring:metric-graph
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (dependsOnService) - the Query Service dashboard's Slow Queries feature is explicitly sourced from live system keyspaces rather than the metrics pipeline itself; service:query-service is an existing extraction-layer concept (server/learn/services-and-indexes/services/query-service.json), not yet promoted to concepts/
relations.evidence: Data on slow queries is sourced from [system keyspaces](../../n1ql/n1ql-intro/sysinfo.md#querying-keyspaces), which provide real-time monitoring details and statistics about individual queries and the Query Service.

notable_absence.finding: No plan-gating language anywhere on this page - Monitoring dashboards are available to all operational cluster plans, including Basic, which is exactly the fallback this batch's other pages (health-advisor.md, configure-*-integration.md) point Basic-plan users toward. This is the plan-agnostic baseline monitoring tier, confirming (by omission) the plan-gated tiers built on top of it (Health Advisor, alert integrations).

cross_component_finding: Recurrence of the known server-version-string/`/server/...`-path anomaly: this page links twice to `/server/current/n1ql/n1ql-manage/monitoring-n1ql-query.md` for Slow Queries thresholds ('Couchbase Capella categorizes slow queries as those running longer than 1000ms' with the definition sourced from a server/current/ page, and 'Capella only retains the most recent 4,000 completed requests... with run times longer than 1000 ms' likewise sourced from server/current/) - the same pattern flagged in reconciliation.md as `capella-pages-cite-server-versions` (server/ content reused with the product name substituted, or in this case, its numeric limits cited via a live link into server/current/ rather than restated as Capella's own documented behavior). Flagged as recurrence, not a new anomaly.
